subject: Temporary throughput bump for BrightLane campaign
messages:
From: Samir Patel <samir@brightlane.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-02T09:14:00-07:00
Subject: Request: Temporary throughput bump for BrightLane campaign

Hi Olga,

Quick note — we have a major marketing push scheduled the week of May 10th and expect a 6x spike in inference volume for user-facing flows. Can Redwood provide a short-term throughput elevation (QPS and token quota) for ~2–3 weeks? Our options team wants to avoid surprises on overage charges.

Two asks:
- A clear commercial option for a temporary quota bump (duration, prepay vs post-pay, and effective overrun rate)
- A simple amendment/PO path so our procurement can sign off quickly

We can commit to an estimated uplift of ~1.2B extra tokens over three weeks if that helps with pricing. Attaching current invoice snapshot.

Thanks — Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform
BrightLane.ai

Attachment: invoice_snapshot_may.pdf (pdf)
From: olga.petrov@redwood.com
To: ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: samir@brightlane.ai
Date: 2027-05-02T11:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary throughput bump for BrightLane campaign

Thanks for the heads-up, Samir — looping in Ben (commercial), Laura (finance) and Markus (legal) to put a quick, signable path together.

Ben / team: our ask from BrightLane is a 2–3 week uplift starting ~May 10 with an estimated +1.2B tokens. They want clarity on overrun pricing and a PO flow. Can we propose:
- Option A: 3-week provisional uplift with a one-time prepay credit for forecasted uplift at a 10% discount to the list overrun rate; any consumption above the prepay credited amount billed at a capped overrun rate (X% above committed unit price).
- Option B: No prepay — elevated soft-quota for 3 weeks at a temporarily reduced overrun rate if they sign an amendment + PO.

Laura: which option is preferable for cash flow / accounting?
Markus: if we do an amendment, can we get a short DocuSign template and confirm SOW/PO acceptance language?

Samir: will circulate a short estimate for the uplift (tokens/day) if helpful.

—Olga
Olga Petrov
Senior Account Executive
Redwood Inference
From: ben.carter@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com
Cc: samir@brightlane.ai
Date: 2027-05-03T08:27:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary throughput bump for BrightLane campaign

All,

Proposed commercial (quick summary):
- Duration: 3 weeks (May 10 — May 30)
- Capacity: provisional uplift to cover estimated +1.2B tokens
- Commercials: Option 1 (Prepay): BrightLane prepays for 1.0B tokens at a 12% discount to standard hosted overrun pricing; any usage above 1.0B during the uplift billed at a capped overrun rate equal to standard list + 5%. Unused prepay credits roll into next invoice as account credit for up to 90 days.
- Option 2 (Amendment w/ PO): No prepay, but if they sign the short amendment and provide PO, we provide the uplift and bill actual overrun at list + 8% with a one-time 5% volume rebate if total overrun stays below 15% of the forecasted uplift.

Rationale: prepay protects Redwood from sudden spikes (helps capacity planning) while offering BrightLane upside on price. Option 2 is easier for procurement if they can’t prepay.

Attachment: proposed_term_sheet.pdf (pdf) — I’ve included line-item math and a sample credit schedule.

Laura: confirm the accounting treatment for the prepay credit and whether we can allow 90-day rollover. Markus: I’ll need a one-paragraph amendment you can sign off on, ideally DocuSign-ready.

Ben Carter
Commercial Lead, Enterprise Sales
Redwood Inference
From: markus.klein@redwood.com
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Cc: samir@brightlane.ai
Date: 2027-05-04T10:48:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary throughput bump for BrightLane campaign

Thanks — short path from legal:
- I’ve drafted a 1-page amendment that: names the uplift window, defines the prepay credit mechanics, and ties PO acceptance to invoicing. No substantive SLA changes.
- I prefer Option 1 for predictability; Option 2 is okay if the finance team takes the billing risk.
- Sending DocuSign-ready doc: "redwood_amendment_docusign.docx" — we should: (a) confirm the exact token uplift figure to avoid ambiguity, (b) include a single sentence around billing/carry-forward of unused credits (90 days).

Small legal ask for procurement acceptance: BrightLane must include a PO number on the DocuSign envelope or our AP team will not accept it as payment authorization. I added a field for PO#.

Markus Klein
Senior Counsel
Redwood Inference
From: Samir Patel <samir@brightlane.ai>
To: olga.petrov@redwood.com, ben.carter@redwood.com, markus.klein@redwood.com, laura.bennett@redwood.com
Date: 2027-05-05T16:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Request: Temporary throughput bump for BrightLane campaign

Team — thanks, this is great. BrightLane will take Option 2 (amendment + PO) to avoid moving cash. Procurement issued PO BG-7721 and attached it here.

We confirm estimated uplift numbers: ~1.2B tokens total across May 10–30. Please confirm effective start date and that the amendment will be routed for signature today. We’ll aim to have PO accepted and signed by EOD May 6.

Attachment: BrightLane_PO_0510.pdf (pdf)

—Samir
Samir Patel
Head of Platform
BrightLane.ai
